title: Remote monthly levels gave no clear three-month sea-level forecast gain at San Diego and Fremantle in 1990-2024
abstract: We tested whether recent level at the other gauge improves monthly sea-level prediction at San Diego and Fremantle after local history and ENSO are known. Expanding linear fits used only training outcomes at or before the origin. The three-month test had 378 matched target months per site in 1990-2024. Adding two remote levels gave an equal-site mean MSE reduction of -0.28%, with conditional 95% five-year block limits of -1.32% to +0.66%. All planned mean checks included zero. This extends an earlier partner-gauge test to a different pair linked to Pacific climate. It does not establish a physical cause or absence of remote information. Two sites, revised data, common-case selection, simple response models, and intervals conditional on saved errors limit inference. Code, source hashes, retrieval instructions, aggregate errors, uncertainty draws, and a numerical audit are preserved. Source records and monthly prediction tables remain external.

display.caption: Equal-site MSE reduction from remote monthly levels. All conditional 95% mean intervals include zero. The primary lead is three calendar months.
